shadows.name: printed-underline

motion.name: reading-ruler

components.css: :host{--paper:#f4f7f2;--band:#e3eedf;--ruled:#d3e4cd;--form:#3b6843;--rule:#a8c5a2;--ink:#1a1f1b;--ink-soft:#465049;--red:#ae2219;--line:1.375rem;--sans:Archivo,'Arial Narrow',system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:'Martian Mono',ui-monospace,'Cascadia Mono',Consolas,monospace;}.ds-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-family:var(--sans);font-size:0.9375rem;line-height:var(--line);color:var(--ink);background:var(--paper);}.ds-table th{font-stretch:75%;font-weight:700;font-size:0.75rem;letter-spacing:0.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--form);text-align:left;padding:0 0.75rem calc(var(--line) / 4);border-bottom:1px solid var(--form);}.ds-table td{padding:calc(var(--line) / 2) 0.75rem;vertical-align:top;}.ds-table .n{text-align:right;white-space:nowrap;}.ds-table td.n{font-family:var(--mono);font-stretch:87.5%;font-size:0.8125rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums slashed-zero;}.ds-table .u{color:var(--ink-soft);font-size:0.75em;margin-left:0.35em;}.ds-table .st{font-family:var(--mono);font-stretch:87.5%;font-size:0.75rem;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.04em;text-transform:uppercase;}.ds-table .r{color:var(--red);}.ds-table a{color:inherit;font-weight:600;text-decoration-color:var(--form);text-underline-offset:0.22em;}.ds-table tbody tr{transition:background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1),box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);}.ds-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--band);}.ds-table tbody tr:hover,.ds-table tbody tr:focus-within{background:var(--ruled);box-shadow:inset 0 -2px 0 var(--ink);}.ds-table a:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:2px;}@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.ds-table tbody tr{transition:none;}}

narrative.overview:
Every screen is the morning's exception run, printed on continuous-form line-printer stationery. The metaphor is kept only where it does a job. The bands on alternate rows are there for the reason they were always there: they hold the eye on one row across a wide table. The two inks are provenance. Green is the form, preprinted before any invoice existed: headings, column titles, instructions. Black is what the system printed onto it: vendors, figures, reasons. A second, red ribbon prints only what stopped. Anything else from the paper (tractor holes, tear-off stubs) did no work here and is not here.

The page is dense on purpose and flat on purpose. There are no containers: structure comes from rules printed on the paper (hairline, dashed perforation, accountant's double) and from the printer-line module every vertical measure is cut from. Headings are condensed and green; figures are condensed mono, tabular, right-aligned. It should read as a tool that runs a finance team's week, not a demo of one.

Motion is one moment: hovering or tabbing through a table lays a reading ruler under the row you are on, the way these printouts were read with a ruler under the line. Dark mode is the same report under a dim lamp: the paper goes near-black green, the form ink lightens, the ribbon stays red.
keyCharacteristics: Two inks by provenance: green for the form, black for the print, red only for stops.
Pale green bands on alternate table rows; a darker ruled band plus a 2px ink underline for the row being read.
Printer-line vertical module (1.375rem) and its halves and quarters.
Square corners, rules instead of boxes, no drop shadows.
Condensed grotesque for the form's voice, condensed mono with tabular, slashed-zero numerals for everything printed.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Green is what was on the form before the invoice arrived; black is what the system printed onto it. If a string came from the data, it is black. If it explains the page, it is green.

rules.name: The Red Ribbon Rule
rules.body: Red prints only what stopped (blocked, over, failed, refused), and always beside words that say the same thing. A refusal that is the system working ("not yours", "already decided") is printed in the form's ink, never red.

rules.name: The Column Title Rule
rules.body: Column titles are the form's, even over a column of figures: condensed, green, uppercase, right-aligned over numbers but never set in the mono.

rules.name: The No Bare Number Rule
rules.body: A figure is never printed without its column title or unit. When tables stack on narrow screens, each cell prints its column title beside it.

rules.name: The Rules Not Boxes Rule
rules.body: Group with a printed rule, never with a container. Hairline (1px) separates records, dashed (1px) marks a new page of the run, double (3px) opens a major section or closes a total.

rules.name: The Reading Ruler Rule
rules.body: The one motion: on hover or focus-within, a table row takes the Ruled Band fill and a 2px Print Black underline (`inset 0 -2px 0`), over 150ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`. It is removed under reduced motion. Nothing else animates for effect.

dos: **Do** cut every vertical measure from the printer line (1.375rem), its half or its quarter.
**Do** print every figure in the mono with tabular, slashed-zero numerals, right-aligned, with its unit in Faded Print.
**Do** put the accountant's double rule (3px double, Print Black) under a final figure, and only there among figures.
**Do** pair every red element with words that say the same thing; status is never carried by colour alone.
**Do** keep one active edge: a 2px Print Black outline at 2px offset on every focusable element, never removed.
**Do** mark the current item (nav page, payment station, reading row) with ink and a 2px ink underline.
donts: **Don't** use cards, rounded corners, drop shadows, sidebars, KPI tiles or status pills. The inset 2px underline is a printed rule and is the only shadow value allowed.
**Don't** print a refusal that is the system working ("not yours to decide", "already decided") in red.
**Don't** set a small label above a title; the title says what the page is.
**Don't** set column titles in the mono, even over figures.
**Don't** add motion beyond the reading ruler.
**Don't** make the agent's escalation look authoritative: no fill, no emphasis colour, no border heavier than the dashed perforation.
